posts.name: The Burning Stickman
posts.cooked:
They say the quote on Segmentation Fault is from the fight between Parse and Revenant, just that Revenant was muttering it under his breath.

But in Editors Note 11, they said it was an instance where the art and quote don't match -- that Marc Benedetto said it to her in her backstory.

  • If Revenant didn't know the identities of Setback and Parse until after the company was sold to him after Vengeance, then what's the explanation from Vengeance #4 when he tells Parse that she's fired? More in Parse's episode, but part of the side story going on here is that Kim, having the ability to see connections and weaknesses now, is able to piece together that RevoCorp is owned by Baron Blade and goes to the boss to show him and figure out what's going on. "That's ridiculous!" "But what about all this evidence?" "You shouldn't even have access to those files. I think it goes without saying that you're fired." The flavor text and art on "Segmentation Fault" don't coincide.

So what gives, C+A?

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I could feel the bit where they said "Parse could come up with the right answer but wouldn't have the people skills to convince others she really does know what she's talking about" because that's pretty much one of the main stories of my life. :P (I particularly feel like I end up having to say "I told you so" way too often versus what I would prefer regards actually being allowed to avert problems in the first place.)

Otherwise, though, I supposed it's a thing where I'm both very logical AND extremely moral, and in fiction (and sometimes often real life too) you very often only get to have one or the other, pick one.

So part of me's like "yay another super-analytical but also socially-awkward data-oriented person!" and then you get to the part where she's kind of ruthless and cavalier about arrowing things and then the ambivalence sets in.

Though this is less of a complaint against the character and more just me not being sure how to feel about her.

Edit: Almost forgot to register my shock that apparently Prime War is going to tell the story of the end of the Miststorm universe? D: Geez, what are the Prime Wardens going up against?

TheBazaarClerk:

Ignoring certain unwritten rules that everybody else follows, 

This is sort of me, except it's less that I deliberately ignore unwritten social rules and more that I keep running into the problem that the unwritten social rules make no sense at all compared to the actual observable social rules.

And so then people get mad at me for always coming up with the observable rules instead of the unwritten rules and it's like, "How am I supposed to figure out/follow rules that make literally no sense?" and in turn people seem to react in what looks to me like totally bizarre and random ways.

(Is it possible to only be autistic about social stuff? )

posts.name: The Girl With No Name
posts.cooked:
I have a theory that Parse's murder phase being explained by Asperger's syndrome is partly due to the fact that Asperger's wasn't quite as understood in the mid-nineties (where they went into her background, if I remember correctly), and that her more modern portrayal is kind of an apology for that. Not an apology, but... I suck at words. 

 

Anyway, they didn't answer my question, but I honestly don't mind. It was something very esoteric about which Aboriginal nation she came from. I guessed Wurundjeri, which is the main people whose ancestors occupied what we now call Melbourne; but again, I doubt it's something that the writers (or C and A, for that matter) really would have thought hard about, so I'm not really cut up about it.
